MTL.head: A tough matchup for the Canadiens
MTL.body: Even though Montréal has home-ice advantage and Colorado may be without Makar, the Avalanche have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Canadiens can pull it off if they keep the shots coming.

story.head: Clash of the titans
paras: The Avalanche (11-6-3) lost 4-3 in overtime to Ottawa on Thursday, while the Canadiens (12-3-4) beat Boston 5-2 the same night. Two of the league’s best teams meet. Going in, the Avalanche are third in the Central (tied for 11th in the NHL) and the Habs second in the Atlantic (tied for fifth).

The Avalanche’s record (.625) is about what their chances are worth. The Canadiens’ record (.737) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.563), largely because they’re 7-5 in one-goal games.

The Avalanche get their defensemen shooting (1st), do a lot of their shooting from distance (lowest) and play the league’s fastest games (1st). Colorado has scored 4.05 goals a game, the second most in the league. On the other side, the Canadiens get into more chippy games than almost anyone (2nd), take more penalties than they draw (30th) and give up a lot of dangerous shots (29th). The Canadiens’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Avalanche, and something has to give when the Avalanche’s shooting runs into the Canadiens’ defense.

Martin Nečas (10 G / 14 A / 24 P in 20 GP) leads the Avalanche in scoring, and Artturi Lehkonen (14 G / 5 A / 19 P in 20 GP) has a team-high 14 goals, fifth in the NHL. Cole Caufield (12 G / 6 A / 18 P in 19 GP) is tied for the Canadiens’ scoring lead. Lane Hutson (3 G / 15 A / 18 P in 19 GP) shares it.
Mackenzie Blackwood (10-3-1 / .901 SV% in 14 GS) is in line to start for Colorado. Jacob Fowler (9-1-2 / .926 SV% in 12 GS) has been terrific for Montréal and will likely start.
At home, Martin St. Louis likes to send Caufield, Suzuki and Slafkovský out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Lehkonen, MacKinnon and Nečas.

items.text: Brent Burns is set to play his 1,600th NHL game.
Nick Suzuki has a point in six straight games against Colorado, and 9 points in his last six against them.
The Avalanche are newly without Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team is missing more right now.
The Canadiens are newly without Chris Kreider, and have been without Ivan Demidov and Samuel Montembeault for several games. Jacob Fowler is expected to start.
